title: Book Three · Chapter 126: The Front Shelves
story:
On Monday, Ronan reaches the workshop ten minutes before nine.

He has brought a water bottle and a clean cloth. Mr Sun gives him a pencil and shows him three front shelves.

Finished small pieces go on the top shelf. Work that needs checking stays on the middle one. Loose paper goes below.

Ronan wipes an empty space and starts with the paper.

Some sheets have customer names. Others have sizes or little drawings. He puts the names together, then finds the matching drawings.

Mr Sun comes over to look.

“Keep each customer's papers together,” he says.

Ronan looks at his separate piles. He has made the names easy to find, but the drawings are across the table.

He moves each drawing beside its name.

“Like this?”

“Yes. Put the newest one on top.”

Ronan starts again. After a while, he can see the dates without moving every sheet.

One small drawing has no date at the top. He looks at the bottom and finds it beside the customer's name.

The next sheet has the name in a different place.

He wants every pile to look the same. He turns one drawing sideways, then realises the little shelf is sideways too.

He puts it back.

Mr Sun passes the front table. Ronan shows him the two sheets.

“Can I write the name here as well?”

“On the cover sheet. Leave the customer's drawing clear.”

Ronan finds a plain cover. He puts the papers inside and writes the name where he can see it.

The drawing can stay the right way up. He opens the cover once more to check the date, then puts the newer sheet above the old one.

His next pile is quicker. He still checks each name. At the end, he can open one cover and find the drawing that belongs with it.

A man comes to collect two small shelves. Ronan finds the name but leaves the pieces in place.

“I will get Mr Sun.”

The man waits by the counter. He looks at Ronan's pencil.

“New here?”

“This morning.”

“The pencil too?”

Ronan looks down. It has a very short end.

“The pencil has more experience.”

The man laughs. Mr Sun comes over, checks the papers, and shows him the finished shelves.

Ronan holds the wrapping paper while Mr Sun ties them together. The man tries the weight before he takes the bundle.

When the counter is clear, Ronan puts the remaining sheet in its place. He checks the name once more before he moves to the next pile.

At half past ten, Mr Sun sends him to the bench near the door for a short rest. Ronan drinks his water and watches Dad across the room.

Dad is checking a corner with another worker. He points to the wood, talks, then moves away while the man cuts.

Ronan has seen him work for years. Today he can see the other people and their jobs around him too.

At twelve, he puts the pencil beside the paper box. Mr Sun looks at the front shelves.

“Wednesday,” he says.

Ronan nods. His back is warm and his fingers are grey from the paper.

Outside, he washes his hands at the yard tap. Dad comes to fill his own cup.

“Still talking?” Dad asks.

“The pencil did most of it.”

Dad looks at the grey water and laughs. Ronan dries his hands and takes his bottle home for lunch.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

matching＝相对应的；newest＝最新的；experience＝经验；bundle＝捆好的一包。

## 理解问题

1. Ronan最初怎样分纸？Mr Sun要求改成怎样的次序？
2. 顾客来取小架子时，Ronan有没有自行交付？他具体帮做了什么？

## 读句子

**The pencil has more experience.**

拆开看：The pencil / has / more experience.

这支铅笔／有／更多工作经验。
